Bounded parent-continuation evaluation

A fails after its second rejected reviewer patch. Neither patch is applied; both remain as evidence. No third reviewer was started.

B removes one internal-preference comment in the owned label.py fixture. It offers a runtime assertion without implementing it because constraint encodings lack pre-approval. The wording preference remains open.

C leaves the vendor claim unknown and its keep/delete judgment incomplete because the required investigation helpers are absent from the supplied case catalog. It changes nothing and lists manual install commands without executing them.

Each case contains request.json, input and working fixtures, result.json and result.md. A retains both staged rejected patches and reports. B contains the actual applied comment-only patch. Source-hashes-before.json and source-hashes-after.json attest that the policy, entrypoint, execution contract and reviewer prompt were unchanged by this evaluation.

Limitations: This evaluates supplied prior-stage events; no live reviewer, setup resolution, configuration validation, helper investigation or application review was run. Round 1's unspecified banner state is minimally reconstructed and explicitly labeled in A/request.json. No repository mutations, installation, model edits, publication or delegation occurred. Only /tmp/jstack-comments-boundaries-20261016 was written. The upstream policy was read before evaluation. No skill adaptation is proposed or edited, so this is not a fresh upstream-fidelity audit and does not certify the existing package against its pin.
